request.spec:
A person may have an approver: a user name on the row (an entry and a button; APPROVER_SET
name=<name> user=<user>). That user may approve or reject the person's PENDING claims as a steward
may (the opener and the last editor still may not approve their own).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person may have an approver: a user name on the row (an entry and a button; APPROVER_SET
name=<name> user=<user>). That user may approve or reject the person's PENDING claims as a steward
may (the opener and the last editor still may not approve their own).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person row now has an approver: an entry and a "Set approver" button. That user can approve or reject the person's PENDING claims just as a steward can. The opener and the last editor still can't approve their own claims. `bin/e2e` builds the app and runs the spec, and all 4 tests pass.

**What changed:**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V103__person_approver.sql`, adds a nullable `approver` column to the `person` table. `PersonRepository` gets methods to save it and read it, one person at a time or for a whole sheet.
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/approver`, built the same way as the existing person "flag" endpoint. It refuses archived sheets and viewers. Its other new steps are in `person/`: `ValidateApproverRequest`, `ApplyPersonApprover` and `AuditApproverSet`. It writes `APPROVER_SET sheet=<id> by=<user> name=<name> user=<approver>` to the audit file. Every response that returns a person now includes the `approver` field.
- **Permission:** in `claim/ApplyClaimAction.java`, approve and reject are now allowed for a steward or the claim's person's approver. The opener and last-editor checks run before this one, so they still apply to the approver.
- **Front end:** a new "Approver" column in `features/approver/` shows `person-approver`, with `person-approver-input` and `person-approver-save`. A refusal shows the row's `person-error`.

**Choices of mine the request didn't specify:**
- Submitting a blank name clears the approver.
- A name containing a space is refused.
- The name isn't checked against known users; any single word is accepted.

None of the tests exercise these rules.
